correctness.rationale: Exact radial moments yield the fourth-power convolution identity. Cauchy and the binomial identity give c_0=c_1=1>c_2>=c_k for k>=2 with quantitative gap 1/[2(alpha+1)]. That gap localizes every optimizer to coefficient mass s=O(delta), higher-mode mass H=O(delta^2). A uniform polarized convolution bound justifies the fourth-order normal form, and square completion plus an explicit normalized three-mode trial gives matching upper/lower asymptotics and all optimizer limits. Compactness for r<1 gives norm attainment. A standalone 490-check finite test was executed independently of the logical proof; finite checks do not replace infinite-dimensional estimates.
